Dental Intelligence and Denticon Unite to Streamline Practice Operations PLEASANT GROVE, UT – April 27, 2026 – In a significant move for the dental technology sector, Dental Intelligence today announced the full integration of its powerful Engagement suite with Denticon, the cloud-based practice management system (PMS) from Planet DDS. The integration, which is now live and available to all Denticon users, creates a unified platform designed to eliminate administrative friction, enhance patient relationships, and drive practice growth. For thousands of dental practices, this partnership addresses a persistent challenge: the fragmentation of essential software tools. By creating a seamless, two-way data sync between one of the industry's leading patient engagement platforms and a dominant cloud-based PMS, the collaboration promises to deliver a more cohesive and efficient operational experience without the need for manual data entry or complex workarounds. Streamlining the Modern Dental Office The primary promise of this integration is the reduction of what dental office managers often call "busy work"—the administrative tasks that consume valuable time and divert focus from patient care. Dental Intelligence’s Engagement suite is a comprehensive toolkit built to automate and simplify these critical functions. With the new integration, Denticon users can now leverage features like 24/7 Online Scheduling to fill their calendars automatically and Digital Forms that patients can complete from home, which then sync directly into the PMS. This eliminates the cumbersome process of printing, scanning, and manually entering patient information, preventing front-desk bottlenecks and ensuring data accuracy. Other key features now available to Denticon practices include automated appointment reminders and confirmations, which are proven to drastically reduce no-shows, and advanced communication tools like TouchPoints™, an automation engine for recalls and patient reactivation campaigns. The suite also includes Team Tasks and Team Chat to improve internal coordination, ensuring that patient follow-ups and critical operational duties are never missed. By automating these workflows, dental teams can reclaim hours in their day, allowing them to focus on higher-value activities like treatment plan coordination and direct patient interaction. “Denticon practices have been asking for this, and we’re excited to deliver,” said Dan Larsen, Chief Product Officer at Dental Intelligence. “Engagement will help so many teams cut down on the busy work so they can focus on dentistry.” Redefining the Patient Journey Beyond internal efficiency, the integration is poised to fundamentally elevate the patient experience. In an era where consumers expect digital convenience in every aspect of their lives, from banking to retail, healthcare is no exception. The Dental Intelligence suite modernizes the patient journey from the first point of contact to the final payment. Features like two-way texting allow for quick, convenient communication, while virtual check-in kiosks reduce waiting room congestion and create a safer, more streamlined intake process. The platform also includes integrated Payments, simplifying the collections process for both the practice and the patient with digital and mobile payment options. Furthermore, an Online Reviews module helps practices manage their digital reputation by making it easy to solicit and monitor patient feedback. By providing a seamless, user-friendly experience, practices can significantly boost patient satisfaction, which is a key driver of retention and referrals. This focus on the patient journey transforms routine appointments into positive, memorable interactions, fostering long-term loyalty in a competitive market. A Strategic Alliance in a Competitive Tech Landscape This partnership represents a powerful strategic alignment between two major players in the dental software industry. Planet DDS has established Denticon as a leading PMS, particularly among fast-growing Dental Support Organizations (DSOs) and multi-location practices, with a footprint of over 14,500 practices. Dental Intelligence, meanwhile, is widely recognized for its best-in-class analytics and patient engagement solutions. By joining forces, they create a compelling offering that directly challenges other all-in-one platforms and standalone engagement tools. The demand for integrated systems has never been higher, especially among larger dental groups that require scalable, standardized technology to manage complex operations. This integration directly answers that call by connecting essential tools without the headaches that often accompany third-party software. “We hear the same thing from our customers every week: they want their practice management solution to work with the tools they already use, without workarounds or manual data entry,” noted Nathan James, Chief Product Officer at Planet DDS. “That’s what this integration delivers. Dental Intelligence Engagement now plugs directly into Denticon, and practices get the benefit without the usual integration headaches.” The Future is Data-Driven: Analytics on the Horizon While the immediate benefits center on patient engagement and operational efficiency, the partnership’s long-term vision extends even further. The press release revealed that additional analytics capabilities for Denticon users are planned for future releases within the Dental Intelligence platform. This signals a deeper, more strategic phase of the collaboration. Dental Intelligence built its reputation on its powerful analytics engine, which transforms raw practice data into actionable insights for improving production, collections, and clinical performance. The future integration of these advanced analytics with Denticon's rich data will provide practice leaders with an unprecedented, 360-degree view of their business. This will empower them to track key performance indicators, identify hidden revenue opportunities, and make data-driven decisions with confidence. For Denticon practices, this means the tools to not only run their practice efficiently day-to-day but also to strategize for long-term growth and profitability, truly enabling them to Practice Smarter™.

data.title: 2026 Dental Industry Statistics & Market Trends
data.ai_summary: The dental industry in 2026 reports a total revenue of $179.4 billion in the United States, with ongoing growth and expansion into new market segments. However, practices face significant operational challenges such as staffing shortages, insurance issues, and rising costs, leading to a decline in dentist confidence.
data.author: Patientdesk Team
data.full_text:
The dental industry reached $179.4 billion in 2026, but faces major challenges. 54.2% of practices struggle with staffing shortages while dentist confidence dropped to 53%.

The dental industry in 2026 presents a fascinating paradox: robust market growth alongside significant operational challenges. While the sector continues to expand and evolve, dental practices are grappling with unprecedented staffing shortages, insurance complexities, and rising overhead costs.

Market Size and Growth Projections

According to IBISWorld, the market size of the Dentists industry in the United States reached $179.4 billion in 2026. This substantial figure reflects the dental industry's resilience and continued growth trajectory.

The broader dental services market shows even more impressive numbers. Fortune Business Insights reports that the dental services market is expected to reach $471.47 billion in 2026, growing from $440.81 billion in 2025. This 7% year-over-year growth demonstrates the industry's expanding reach and increasing demand for dental care.

Within specific segments, cosmetic dentistry continues to drive significant growth. The cosmetic dental market is projected to reach $18-20 billion by 2026, up from approximately $11.5 billion in 2022, according to Imagine Your Smile. This nearly doubled market size in four years highlights the growing consumer interest in aesthetic dental procedures.

Confidence Levels and Industry Sentiment

Despite strong market fundamentals, dentist confidence has notably declined. The American Dental Association found that only 53% of dentists felt very or somewhat confident in their practice at the end of 2025, compared to 68% twelve months prior.

This 15-percentage-point drop in confidence reflects the mounting operational pressures facing dental practices. The decline comes at a time when external market conditions suggest growth opportunities, indicating that internal practice management challenges are weighing heavily on practitioners' outlooks.

Interestingly, DSO-affiliated dentists appear more optimistic about taking action in 2026 compared to non-DSO dentists. These practitioners are more likely to make major equipment purchases, invest in new software, and expand their staff, suggesting that larger organizational structures may provide resources to navigate current challenges more effectively.

Top Challenges Facing Dental Practices

The ADA Health Policy Institute identified the three most pressing challenges facing dental practices in 2026:

Insurance Issues (55.3%)

More than half of dental practices cite insurance-related problems as their primary concern. These issues include complex reimbursement processes, declining reimbursement rates, and increasing administrative burden associated with insurance claims processing.

However, there are positive developments in dental benefits. Ameritas notes that higher annual dental benefit maximums ranging from $2,500 to $5,000 are becoming more common, with shorter waiting periods and expanded coverage for implants and adult orthodontia.

Staffing Shortages (54.2%)

Staffing challenges represent the second-largest concern for dental practices. Despite high graduation rates from dental hygiene programs and three steady months of job additions, dentists continue reporting difficulty recruiting and hiring staff.

The staffing crisis is particularly acute for dental hygienists. As Dr. Vilas Sastry, CEO of Teledentistry.com, explains: "The chronic shortage of hygienists is forcing the industry to move beyond traditional staffing, increasingly relying on teledentistry for virtual triage and AI-driven automation."

To address these challenges, many practices are turning to AI-powered dental practice automation solutions that can handle routine administrative tasks, allowing existing staff to focus on patient care and reducing the burden on understaffed teams.

Overhead Costs (41.5%)

Rising overhead costs round out the top three concerns. These encompass everything from equipment and technology investments to facility costs and regulatory compliance expenses.

Despite cost pressures, investment in practice improvements continues. The ADA data shows that 42.3% of dentists plan to add staff in 2026, and many are considering major equipment purchases and software upgrades.

Technology Transformation and Market Segments

The dental industry is undergoing significant technological transformation. According to Becker's Dental Review, "Technology integration is transforming dental practices from static physical locations into agile, technology-integrated hubs with AI-driven automation and teledentistry."

This technological shift is creating new opportunities for practices to improve efficiency and patient outcomes. Solutions like automated patient follow-up systems are helping practices maintain consistent patient communication while reducing administrative burden.

In terms of market segmentation, Coherent Market Insights reports that dental clinics hold 35.4% of the market share in 2026 in the end user segment. This dominance reflects the continued preference for traditional dental clinic settings, even as alternative care models emerge.

Payment Trends and Financial Dynamics

Patient payment patterns reveal important insights about dental care accessibility and practice revenue models. The out-of-pocket payment segment dominates with 61.85% market share in 2026, driven by limited reimbursement policies for cosmetic procedures, according to Fortune Business Insights.

This heavy reliance on out-of-pocket payments highlights both opportunities and challenges. While practices can maintain higher margins on self-pay procedures, they must also navigate patient affordability concerns and payment collection challenges.

The dentures market provides another lens into demographic and financial trends. Savage Smiles projects the dentures market will climb from $1.67 billion in 2025 to $1.82 billion in 2026, reflecting an aging population and continued demand for restorative dental solutions.

Operational Metrics and Performance Benchmarks

Mike Huffaker, Chief Revenue Officer of Planet DDS, emphasizes the importance of data-driven practice management: "Dental leaders are looking for signals they can trust, and the strongest ones are in the day-to-day operational metrics. By comparing their own performance against industry averages, leaders can quickly see where they're ahead, where they're falling behind, and where focused changes will have the biggest impact."

The Planet DDS 2026 Dental Industry Outlook provides valuable benchmarks based on data from over 15,000 practices, helping practitioners understand how their performance compares to industry standards.

Future Outlook and Strategic Considerations

Despite current challenges, the dental industry's fundamental growth drivers remain strong. An aging population, increased awareness of oral health's connection to overall wellness, and growing demand for cosmetic procedures continue to fuel market expansion.

Practices that successfully navigate 2026's challenges will likely be those that:

Embrace technology solutions to address staffing shortages and improve efficiency

to address staffing shortages and improve efficiency Optimize revenue cycles through better patient communication and follow-up processes

through better patient communication and follow-up processes Invest strategically in equipment and software that provide measurable ROI

in equipment and software that provide measurable ROI Focus on operational metrics to identify improvement opportunities

The integration of practice management software solutions becomes increasingly critical as practices seek to streamline operations and maximize productivity with existing staff.

"The dental workforce is prioritizing extreme flexibility and tech-enabled, hybrid care models," notes Dr. Vilas Sastry, highlighting the industry's evolution toward more adaptive service delivery models.

Conclusion

The 2026 dental industry statistics paint a picture of a sector in transition. While market fundamentals remain strong with $179.4 billion in revenue and continued growth projections, operational challenges are testing practice resilience.

Success in this environment requires balancing traditional dental care excellence with modern operational efficiency. Practices that leverage technology to address staffing shortages, optimize patient communication, and streamline administrative processes will be best positioned to thrive despite current headwinds.

The industry's evolution toward technology-integrated, data-driven operations represents both a challenge and an opportunity. Those who adapt quickly and strategically will emerge stronger, while those who resist change may struggle with the mounting operational pressures that define today's dental landscape.

data.title: Top Cloud-Based Practice Management Software for Dental Practices
data.ai_summary: This article is a buyer's guide comparing four cloud-based dental practice management software platforms: CareStack, Curve Dental, Denticon (by Planet DDS), and Dentrix Ascend (by Henry Schein One). The comparison evaluates each platform across features, user reviews, pricing transparency, AI capabilities, multi-location support, and learning curves to help dental practices evaluate cloud PMS options. The article also advises that cloud adoption requires reliable IT infrastructure, noting that internet dependency and potential outages (such as AWS disruptions) present operational risks that practices must plan for before transitioning from server-based systems.
data.full_text:
Top Cloud-Based Practice Management Software for Dental Practices

So, you’re considering making the switch to a cloud-based practice management software for your dental practice. That’s great and we clearly understand the intrigue... especially because cloud is all the rage these days. But with a crowded market — and every vendor website saying the same things: all-in-one, intuitive, cloud-native, scalable. It can get a little overwhelming. So we did the digging for you. We looked at four of the most talked-about cloud-based practice management systems right now — CareStack, Curve Dental, Denticon, and Dentrix Ascend — and put together an honest, non-biased breakdown: what each system does, what real users are saying in verified reviews, and who each one is genuinely the best fit for. And, as a dental IT provider who has experience troubleshooting and working with cloud PMS... we’ve included some critical considerations as you explore moving your dental practice to a cloud practice management system. There's no ranked list (their in alphabetical order) or winner here. The right PMS for a private general dental practice in Phoenix looks very different from the right solution for a 10-location dental organization on the East Coast.

Looking for a broader dental practice management software comparison that includes server-based or hybrid systems like Dentrix, Eaglesoft, and Open Dental? We covered those - including a full list of dental software programs across deployment types - in our previous article: Top Practice Management Software for Dental Practices. This article focuses specifically on cloud-first solutions for practices ready to leave the server behind. What to Look for in a Cloud-Based Dental PMS Before we get into the individual systems, here are the factors worth weighing as you compare: True cloud vs. cloud-hosted: Is it built for the cloud from the ground up, or is it a legacy system running through a remote desktop?

Ease of use and training time: A powerful system no one knows how to use is a liability, not an asset.

Integrations: Does it work with your imaging software, payment processor, and patient communication tools... or will you be managing a patchwork of add-ons?

Reporting and analytics: Can you get the numbers you need without needing a degree in data science to run a report?

Support quality: What does onboarding look like? What happens when something goes wrong at 3PM on a Wednesday?

Scalability: Will this system grow with you, or will you outgrow it in two years?

Total cost of ownership: Monthly fees are just the beginning. Factor in onboarding, training, add-ons, and data export.

Data portability: If you ever need to switch, can you get your patient records out without a fight? Whether you're new to evaluating dental software programs or you're coming off a legacy system and ready to modernize, these criteria apply regardless of which platform you're considering. CareStack Website: carestack.com

G2 Rating: 4.7/5 (176 reviews)

Software Advice Rating: 4.8/5 (189 reviews) Overview CareStack is an all-in-one, cloud-based dental practice management platform built to serve everything from single-office practices to large, enterprise-level DSOs. The software covers scheduling, clinical charting, treatment planning, billing, revenue cycle management (RCM), patient communications, and analytics — all without the need for third-party add-ons. More than 2,500 dental practices across the U.S. use CareStack. It holds the #1 ranking on G2 for dental practice management software, is certified in HIPAA, SOC 2 Type 2, and ISO 27001:2022, and has been the subject of a Forrester Total Economic Impact™ study that suggests the platform can pay for itself within six months for multi-location practices. CareStack has also been actively expanding its AI capabilities — including AI-driven telephony (VoiceStack™) and AI-powered imaging analysis (Aeka™). What CareStack Users Say "I have been working with CareStack for over 4 years, and the team is amazing — very professional and knowledgeable. The PMS offers comprehensive systems that enable practices to grow both internally and externally, making it an excellent solution for DSOs." — G2 Verified Review "There is a bit of a learning curve at first because the system has so many features. Once you get used to it, though, it becomes much easier to navigate." — G2 Verified Review Pros Truly all-in-one: scheduling, charting, billing, patient communications, RCM, and analytics in a single platform with no required add-ons

Strong multi-location capabilities: centralized reporting and cross-practice operations from one dashboard

Excellent customer support and onboarding: consistently cited as a differentiator in user reviews

Active product development: users report seeing their feature requests implemented

AI-powered growth tools available as part of the ecosystem (VoiceStack™, Aeka™) Cons Steeper learning curve: the depth of features requires meaningful investment in training, especially for teams new to cloud software

Implementation timeline: onboarding can take approximately two months, and some features have been flagged as still "in development" at go-live

Billing workflows can feel multi-step: some users note that billing processes require more clicks than comparable systems

Pricing requires a custom quote: not publicly listed, which makes early budgeting harder

Dependent on internet connectivity: like all cloud systems, a downed connection means disrupted workflow until it's restored Best Suited For CareStack is an excellent fit for growth-oriented practices — whether that's a single office planning to expand, a multi-location group looking to standardize operations, or a DSO that needs enterprise-level visibility and scalability. If your goal is to reduce your vendor count and gain real-time cross-location reporting, CareStack deserves a close look. That said, if your team is small and you need to be up and running quickly without a significant learning curve, the feature depth may feel like more than you need right now. Curve Dental Website: curvedental.com

G2 Rating: 4.6/5 (165 reviews)

Software Advice Rating: 4.4/5 (285 reviews) Overview Curve Dental is one of the original cloud-native dental practice management platforms — built for the cloud from day one, not adapted to it after the fact. This means the system was designed around the realities of browser-based access, mobile flexibility, and continuous delivery of updates — not retrofitted from a legacy product. Trusted by over 80,000 dental professionals across practices of all sizes, Curve offers a comprehensive suite: scheduling, charting, billing, patient intake, treatment planning, automated insurance verification, membership plans, and dashboard reporting — all in one platform. The company also claims customers report up to 20% higher collections, 25% more new patients, and 30% better case acceptance after adopting the system. Curve has also introduced a Curve Mobile experience and continues to integrate AI partners like Pearl and Bola AI for imaging and treatment acceptance improvements. What Curve Dental Users Say “I love using Curve Hero—it makes managing our dental office so much smoother and more organized. The cloud-based system is fast, intuitive, and keeps everything from scheduling to billing perfectly streamlined.” — Software Advice Verified Review “Main benefit I’ve found with Curve is that it is pretty intuitive, which makes it easy to train people who have not used the program. However, we have had issues with rotating outages on Curve for the past year...” — Curve User | Reddit (r/Dentistry - Cloud Based PMS guidance) Pros Clean, intuitive interface: consistently rated easy to learn, with minimal onboarding time

Strong patient engagement tools: automated reminders, two-way texting, SmartFill for wait-list management

Competitive pricing: one of the more accessible entry points among cloud platforms

Highly rated customer support: a consistent highlight in user reviews

Curve Mobile: browser-based mobile access for on-the-go schedule and patient management Cons Reporting depth: some users report that reporting feels less sophisticated compared to enterprise systems, particularly for multi-location analytics

Limited specialty customization: may not meet the complex charting needs of orthodontists, periodontists, or oral surgeons without add-ons

Cloud-only which means full internet dependency

Insurance estimate accuracy: some users note occasional inaccuracies in insurance estimates

Less customizable than open-source or enterprise-level alternatives Best Suited For Curve Dental is an excellent choice for independent practices, dental startups, and small-to-mid-sized multi-location groups that want a modern, polished, and easy-to-use system without the complexity of enterprise software. If minimizing training time, reducing IT costs, and getting staff up and running quickly are priorities, Curve consistently delivers. It's also worth noting for practices coming off server-based systems like Eaglesoft or legacy Dentrix — Curve's user experience tends to feel like a natural leap forward without the steep learning curve of more feature-heavy platforms. Denticon by Planet DDS Website: planetdds.com/denticon

G2 Rating: 4.7/5 (74 reviews)

Software Advice Rating: 4.5/5 (112 reviews) Overview Denticon, developed by Planet DDS, is a cloud-based practice management system built specifically for multi-location dental groups and DSOs. Unlike platforms that started as single-practice solutions and scaled up, Denticon was designed from the beginning to handle the operational complexity of enterprise dental organizations — centralized scheduling, cross-location reporting, multi-specialty workflows, and consolidated RCM at scale. Used by more than 13,000 dental practices, including notable DSO brands like Park Dental, Smile Brands, D4C, and Dental Care Alliance, Denticon positions itself as the operational backbone for high-growth dental businesses. The platform includes a full suite of clinical, front office, and reporting tools, as well as newer additions like AI Voice Perio charting, AI Voice Restorative charting, and AI Assist for proactive patient treatment insights. Planet DDS also offers Apteryx XVWeb — a cloud-based dental imaging solution that integrates directly with Denticon, providing a companion to the practice management platform. What Denticon Users Say "In the last 10 years of using Planet DDS, we have grown from 2 to 11 locations. The ease of use of the product is unmatched. The conversion process is seamless, and the support team is phenomenal." — G2 Verified Review Pros Purpose-built for multi-location and DSO operations: centralized visibility, reporting, and management across all locations from a single platform

Comprehensive RCM tools: batch claims, automated eligibility verification (AutoEligibility), 835 auto-posting, and revenue dashboards

Strong implementation and data conversion support: Planet DDS has experience converting data from nearly every PMS

Morning Huddle dashboard: a standout feature that helps teams start the day aligned on production goals and schedule priorities

Proven track record with enterprise clients: 20+ years in market, with large DSO references Cons Interface can feel dated: multiple users note the UI could benefit from a visual refresh, though Planet DDS acknowledges ongoing work here

Analytics learning curve: while reporting is powerful, some users find the analytics setup complex to configure correctly

Not ideal for solo or small single-location practices: the feature depth and complexity is calibrated for larger organizations Best Suited For Denticon is the right platform for multi-location dental groups, growing DSOs, and enterprise dental organizations that need a cloud-based system capable of handling real operational scale. If you're managing multiple providers and locations, need centralized RCM, and are evaluating against other DSO-grade platforms, Denticon belongs on your shortlist. For smaller, independent single-location practices, the complexity and pricing model may be more than what you need. Lighter, more accessible platforms like Curve Dental or CareStack may serve you better. Dentrix Ascend Website: dentrixascend.com

G2 Rating: 4.3/5 (18 reviews)

Software Advice Rating: 4.1/5 (234 reviews) Overview Dentrix Ascend is the cloud-based evolution of Dentrix — one of the most established names in dental practice management software. Built by Henry Schein One, Ascend takes the brand recognition and deep dental industry roots of legacy Dentrix and moves them into a fully cloud-native environment. The platform covers scheduling, billing, clinical charting, imaging, AI-powered diagnostics, patient communications, and real-time analytics. Ascend has also recently added features like Reserve with Google integration (allowing new patients to book directly through search results), AI-powered call summaries, Voice Notes for hands-free charting documentation, and automated insurance eligibility verification. Over 80,000 clinicians, office managers, and staff use Dentrix Ascend today, with 83% of insurance claims processed annually through the platform. Ascend is not a direct cloud port of legacy Dentrix. It's a rebuilt product with its own workflows — so even longtime Dentrix users may face a learning adjustment. What Dentrix Ascend Users Say “I love how easy Dentrix Ascend is to navigate. It allows me to efficiently move from the patient side to the prescription side and also manages the clinic side seamlessly." — G2 Verified Review “The layout isn't intuitive, and getting meaningful, relevant data often feels like a complex puzzle — honestly, you'd need a PhD in Power Reporting just to make it useful." — Software Advice Verified Review Pros True cloud platform: no servers, no VPNs, accessible from any device with internet

Strong brand trust: built by Henry Schein One, a well-established player in dental technology

AI-powered tools: built-in AI imaging analysis, Voice Notes, and call summaries

Reserve with Google: enables online booking directly from Google search results

Active feature development — Henry Schein One listens to user feedback and regularly releases updates Cons Reporting complexity: multiple users cite the "Power Reporting" feature as unintuitive and difficult to use effectively

Limited third-party integrations at speed: integrations with tools like GoTo or Weave can take longer than expected

Pricing opacity: pricing is not publicly listed; custom quotes required

No dedicated mobile app: browser-based mobile access works, but there's no native iOS or Android app

Data migration challenges: some users report that migrating existing patient data into Ascend was time-consuming Best Suited For Dentrix Ascend is a strong option for practices that already know and trust the Dentrix brand but are ready to move away from on-premise infrastructure. It's particularly well-suited for practices of all sizes that want a clean cloud experience with built-in AI clinical tools, solid security credentials, and the backing of a major industry vendor. One G2 reviewer noted that Ascend supported 280% organizational growth over four years — so for practices in an active growth phase, it's worth a serious look. But, if extensive custom reporting or deep third-party integrations are critical to your workflow, it's worth demoing those specific features carefully before committing. Dental Practice Management Software Comparison: Cloud-Based Systems at a Glance CareStack Curve Dental Denticon Dentrix Ascend G2 Rating 4.7/5 (176) 4.6/5 (165) 4.7/5 (74) 4.3/5 (18) Software Advice Rating 4.8/5 (189) 4.4/5 (285) 4.5/5 (112) 4.1/5 (234) Best Suited For Growth-focused practices & DSOs Startups, independent & small-mid groups Multi-location groups & DSOs Practices familiar with Dentrix; all sizes AI Features VoiceStack™, Aeka™ Pearl & Bola AI partners AI Voice Perio/Restorative, AI Assist AI imaging, Voice Notes Multi-Location Support Strong Moderate Built for it Strong Learning Curve Moderate-High Low-Moderate Moderate-High Moderate Support Reputation Highly rated Highly rated Mixed Generally positive 5 Questions to Ask Before You Choose a Cloud PMS for Your Dental Practice Choosing the best dental practice management software for your practice isn't just about feature checkllists - it's about finding the right fit for how your team works. Before you schedule a demo, get clear on your own answers to these questions: What does "all-in-one" mean to your practice specifically?

Every vendor uses this phrase. What does your practiceactually need in one system — and what are you happy to manage with a best-in-class third-party tool? What does your growth plan look like in the next 3–5 years?

Ifyou're planning to add locations, bring on associate dentists, or eventually pursue a dental organization structure, your PMS needs to be able to grow with you before you outgrow it. What are your staff'stechnical comfort levels?

A feature-rich system that your team struggles to use is an expensive liability. Honest conversations about training time and learning curves matter more than demos. What reporting do you need,and how often?

If you review production, collections, and AR weekly, make sure the system can generate those reports in a way your team can realistically use. Ask to see the actual reporting interface... not just a screenshot. What happens to your data if you ever need to switch?

It's not a fun question, butit's a necessary one. Ask each vendor directly: Can I export my patient records, images, and notes? Is there a fee? How long does it take? Their answer will tell you a lot. Before You Make the Switch - Your IT Setup Matters Here's something that doesn't always come up in PMS conversations, but absolutely should: cloud-based software is only as strong as the infrastructure it runs on. And the stakes are real. A thread on r/Dentistry captured it plainly — when an AWS outage took down several cloud-based practice management systems, dental practices that had gone cloud-only were left with two choices: reschedule appointments or revert to paper charting and manually upload everything later. (4) This isn’t a knock on cloud software. It's a reminder that the move to cloud doesn't eliminate infrastructure risk — it shifts it. And if your network, connectivity, and contingency plan aren't solid, you'll feel every gap. We've seen this play out firsthand.

A dental practice came to us mid-evaluation for cloud-based PMS — excited to ditch their aging server, simplify operations, and finally access their data from anywhere. But they wanted to ensure their network could handle the shift. Their existing internet connection was adequate for a server-based workflow, but it wasn’t adequate for a fully cloud-dependent system at peak hours. Here's what we did: We reviewed their options with local internet service providers, negotiated a plan that hit the performance benchmarks they needed — and kept it well within budget. We secured a business-grade, high-speed connection with a failover backup for redundancy. The monthly cost came in lower than what they'd assumed a "real internet upgrade" would require. Then we helped them decommission the old server... properly wiping and disposing of the hardware, migrating the relevant data, and making sure nothing critical was left stranded on-premise. The result? They launched their new cloud PMS with full confidence. And, had a failover connection in place for the moments when the internet (or the cloud) has other plans. Cloud-based practice management software requires a reliable foundation to perform as advertised. Most dental software companies - including the four featured here - design their cloud platforms with the assumption that your network can handle real-time cloud traffic. And that's a fair assumption... if your infrastructure is actually ready for it. Here's what that means in practice: A reliable, high-speed internet connection preferably with a failover or backup connection at each location

Secure, properly configured network infrastructure: especially important for handling of patient data (HIPAA-compliant)

Managed endpoint devices: workstations, tablets, and imaging hardware that stay updated and protected

A clear plan for your existing server (if you’re making the switch from server to cloud): whether that’s decommissioning, repurposing, or replacing it This is the gap we see most often when practices make the leap to cloud-based systems: the PMS decision gets careful attention, and the IT infrastructure gets an afterthought. They're two sides of the same coin. Ready to Make the Move to a Cloud-Based Practice Management Software? Here's a Simple Plan to Get Started If you're seriously evaluating a cloud-based PMS upgrade, here's a straightforward path forward: Narrow to two or three options based on your practice size, growth goals, and the factors most important to your team. Request live demos... not recorded ones. Walk through real workflows: scheduling an appointment, submitting a claim, running a production report. Talk to current users and ask the vendor for references from practices similar to yours. What was onboarding really like? How's support six months in? Assess your IT infrastructure before you commit to get a clear picture of your network reliability, security posture, and hardware readiness. Review the full contract to understand the total cost of ownership, data portability rights, and what's included vs. what costs extra. Market Driver Insights: The Impact of Recent Advances on the Dental Practice Management Software Market Dental Practice Management Software Market The dental practice management software sector is poised for significant expansion in the coming years, driven by technological advancements and evolving demands within the dental healthcare industry. Dental Practice Management Tools Market Summary



Dental practice management tools are specialized software solutions designed for dental clinics, hospital dentistry departments, and multi-location dental groups. These platforms serve as the operational backbone of modern dental practices, integrating appointment scheduling, electronic health records, billing, treatment planning, imaging management, and patient communications into a unified digital ecosystem. Their core purpose is to enhance clinical efficiency, elevate patient experience, standardize workflows, and provide actionable business intelligence for informed decision-making.



Market Outlook



The global dental practice management tools market is projected to reach USD 3.51 billion by 2032, growing at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 9.5%. This robust growth reflects the accelerating digital transformation across dental care delivery, driven by rising patient expectations, operational complexity, and the imperative for data-driven practice management.



Competitive Landscape



The market is moderately concentrated, with the top ten global players accounting for approximately 50.0% of total revenue. Key solution providers include Dentrix, Planet DDS, CareStack, Eaglesoft, and Open Dental-each offering differentiated capabilities spanning on-premise deployments, cloud-native architectures, and specialty-specific functionality.



Key Market Drivers



1. Rising Complexity of Dental Practice Operations

Growing consumer awareness of oral health, increasing disposable incomes, and expanded insurance coverage have fueled demand for higher-value dental services-including orthodontics, implants, and aesthetic restorations. Practices have evolved from single-provider, basic-treatment models to multi-provider, multi-service operations. Patient scheduling, clinical documentation, imaging integration, inventory tracking, and insurance billing have become increasingly complex. Traditional manual methods or basic spreadsheet tools can no longer support the accuracy, efficiency, and compliance required, compelling practices to adopt professional management platforms.



2. Patient Experience as a Competitive Differentiator

In the increasingly competitive private dental market, patients evaluate practices not only on clinical outcomes but also on convenience, transparency, and communication quality. Modern management tools enhance patient experience through automated appointment reminders, online booking and payment portals, visualized treatment plans, and structured follow-up protocols. Positive patient experiences drive higher retention rates, referrals, and lifetime value-prompting practice owners to view management software as essential infrastructure for customer relationship management rather than a discretionary expense.



3. Cloud Adoption and Multi-Site Scalability

The rapid expansion of dental group practices and franchised networks has created demand for centralized management capabilities. Headquarters require real-time visibility into patient volumes, provider productivity, inventory levels, and financial performance across multiple locations to optimize resource allocation, ensure brand consistency, and control costs. Legacy on-premise systems cannot deliver this cross-site intelligence. data.title: Dental Launch Radar: Mid-March 2026
data.ai_summary: Three new dental technology products were launched in mid-March 2026, including OsteoGen's Bioactive Crystal Technology for bone grafting and Planet DDS's AI agents for practice management. SciCan also introduced the HYDRIM 112W G4+, an automated instrument washer featuring smart monitoring capabilities to enhance infection control and efficiency.
data.author: Sarah Butkovic
data.full_text:
Industry News Dental Launch Radar: Mid-March 2026 Three new product launches—a bioactive bone graft, alternative to AI front-office agents, and a smart instrument washer—signal how rapidly dental technology is reshaping clinical care and practice work.



Alternative material challenges current regenerative dentistry standard Bioactivity influences many restorative procedures and products when it comes to the rapidly evolving regenerative dental industry. Right now, sintered ceramics make up a large portion of today’s bone graft substitutes. The process invovles fusing particles into dense, ceramic structures to simulate natural bone via high heat.1 OsteoGen’s Bioactive Crystal Technology (BCT) is taking a different approach by forgoing sintering in favor of calcium phosphate crystals comprised of bone-like materials. The company says that circumventing the sintering process allows these crystals to retain bioactive properties because they are not exposed to the high sintering temperatures. The material releases calcium ions that may support osteoblastic differentiation and mineralized matrix deposition during healing. Cited by OsteoGen in their press release, research published in the Journal of Periodontology notes that BCT has 94.4% porosity, which may promote bone formation. The same study also found that BCT has a proliferation rate that is six times greater than xenograft and allograft materials.1 OsteoGen says the goal of this product is to shorten procedure time and simplify the bone grafting process without compromising solid clinical results.1 Bioactive Crystal Technology (BCT) AI workforce taking on front-office tasks Planet DDS, a dental software solutions company, has developed AI-powered workers to streamline front office work for staff members. According to Planet DDS, their AI agents can access live patient data, office schedules, and established workflows and are compatible with dental practice management software (Denticon and Cloud 9).2 The scheduling agent: Reaches out to patients from recall lists, waitlists, and those with unscheduled treatment Fills open schedule time when patients cancel appointments Books appointments Logs each interaction into Denticon or Cloud 9 The confirmation agent: Automates appointment confirmations Verifies patient identity before sharing protected health information Writes confirmation and reschedule outcome In a press release, CEO of Planet DDS Eric Giesecke said these tools are intended to increase practice productivity and relieve team members of time-consuming tasks and help them avoid routine busywork. He said: “DSOs that are scaling face an inherent tension—more locations mean more operational complexity, more communication to manage, and more pressure on teams already stretched thin ... [DentalOS] works alongside human teams so organizations can scale without sacrificing consistency, responsiveness, or the people who make it all work.”2 Instrument washer adds digital monitoring features Infection control company SciCan has debuted an automated instrument washer with a touch screen, LED lights, and customizable features—known as HYDRIM 112W G4+. According to SciCan's website, this model is designed to: Reduce the risk of sharps injuries by minimizing how much you’re handling your instruments Cut instrument cleaning costs by $10,000 a year Allow for more time chairside Clean more instruments per cycle than other washers on the market today The manufacturer notes this instrument washer includes smart technology to keep dental practices running smoothly. It has a touch-screen interface with on-screen instruction tutorials, connectivity to equipment software myCOLTENE, support for troubleshooting and running diagnostics, and a digital log of each cleaning cycle.3 SciCan reports the washer can remove 99.9% of protein residues under tested conditions.3 HYDRIM 112W G4+ instrument washer References: Bioactive Crystal Technology (BCT): the science behind predictable bone regeneration. IRVINE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Planet DDS today unveiled DentalOS™ AI Agents, a new category of AI-powered workers purpose-built to operate within the dental practice management system. DentalOS AI Agents are intelligent, autonomous agents that live inside Denticon and Cloud 9, accessing live patient data, real schedules, and established workflows to complete operational work the way a trained team member would, at any hour, across every location. The first agents target front desk operations, where missed communication directly leads to lost revenue. Today, the average dental practice sees a 15% no-show rate, costing providers more than $150,000 per year in lost production—and 36% of patients who miss appointments say they simply forgot. For DSOs and multi-location groups, these gaps compound across dozens or hundreds of locations. These are solvable problems. The newly announced Confirmation Agent and Scheduling Agent are designed to address these challenges systematically across organizations. But the front desk is only the starting point. Planet DDS will introduce additional AI agent roles throughout 2026 and beyond, building toward a full AI workforce spanning clinical coordination, patient communications, revenue cycle management, and more, all embedded within DentalOS. Denticon and Cloud 9 customers can join the early access waitlist at planetdds.com/ai-agents-early-access. “DSOs that are scaling face an inherent tension—more locations mean more operational complexity, more communication to manage, and more pressure on teams already stretched thin," said Eric Giesecke, CEO of Planet DDS. "We're introducing an entirely new way of using our software by providing access to an AI workforce that lives inside DentalOS, understands the full context of every patient interaction, and works alongside human teams so organizations can scale without sacrificing consistency, responsiveness, or the people who make it all work. The Confirmation and Scheduling Agents we're launching are just the beginning.” Meet the First Two AI Agents for Dental Front Desk Operations Confirmation Agent automates outbound appointment confirmations within a configurable window, helping DSOs reduce no-shows and stabilize provider schedules without increasing staff workload. If a patient can't make it, the agent can reschedule the appointment during the same call using policy-controlled slot search—without creating scheduling risk. It verifies patient identity before sharing protected health information, respects consent and office hours, and writes confirmation and reschedule outcomes back into Denticon and Cloud 9 with full auditability. The Confirmation Agent has been shown to increase appointment confirmation rates by 20–50% from historic baselines, reduce no-shows by 15–30%, and save front desk teams an estimated 60–75% of hours previously spent on manual confirmation workflows. Scheduling Agent keeps schedules full by proactively reaching out to patients from recall lists, waitlists, ASAP lists, and unscheduled treatment, then booking appointments directly into the practice management system. When cancellations occur, the agent triggers time-sensitive outreach to quickly recover open time. It reaches patients through outgoing calls and logs every interaction back into Denticon and Cloud 9, so teams maintain full visibility across locations. "The Confirmation and Scheduling Agents protect production and reduce no-shows, which for DSOs means healthier EBITDA," said Nathan James, Chief Product Officer at Planet DDS. "And this is just the first layer. As we bring AI agents into the revenue cycle, clinical coordination, and beyond, we're building a workforce that strengthens our customers’ business at every level.” How DentalOS AI Agents Work: Real-time access to live schedules and patient records within Denticon and Cloud 9

Independently complete front desk workflows, including appointment confirmations, rescheduling, missed call recovery, and routine patient inquiries

Every DentalOS AI Agent—current and future—connects directly with Denticon and Cloud 9, cloud-based dental practice management platforms by Planet DDS, with real-time access to the same data and workflows human teams rely on every day. This shared foundation enables agents to act with full operational awareness, following each organization's scheduling rules, communication standards, and escalation paths without manual configuration for every interaction. As Planet DDS introduces new agents across additional operational domains, each will inherit the same data and organizational intelligence, allowing DSOs to continue expanding their AI workforce. data.title: Why your revenue cycle management strategy can be a financial liability
data.ai_summary: The author argues that dental service organizations (DSOs) are losing significant revenue—up to 2.9% of production from inaccurate insurance verification alone, and 0.6% to 8% of revenue consumed by manual RCM processes—because they delay modernizing their revenue cycle management systems. The article contends that AI-driven automation can verify insurance eligibility in real time, reduce claim denials, improve cash flow, and enable DSOs to scale operations without proportionally increasing headcount. The author, Stephen Fong, CFO of Planet DDS, advises dental organizations to implement RCM automation proactively to eliminate revenue leakage, protect staff from burnout, and build scalable operations ahead of competitors.
data.author: Stephen Fongfeb
data.full_text:
Here's what keeps me up at night as a chief financial officer: watching dental organizations leave millions on the table because they're waiting for the "right time" to modernize their revenue cycle management (RCM). There is no right time. Every month you delay is another month of denied claims, burned-out staff, and cash flow you'll never recover. The numbers are stark. By some estimates, inaccurate insurance verification alone costs practices up to 2.9% of production -- $29,000 per $1 million in lost revenue. Add manual claims follow-up and denial rework, and you're looking at 0.6% to 8% of revenue consumed by RCM headcount costs. For a DSO doing $100 million annually, that's potentially $8 million in operational drag. Yet I still hear, "We'll get to automation next year." Meanwhile, the cash bleeding continues. Today, the question isn’t whether to adopt automation and AI, but how quickly can practices implement these technologies to stay competitive? Let’s explore why AI-driven RCM tools are fast becoming a make-or-break technology for DSOs and dental groups. The growing burden of traditional RCM Traditionally, RCM processes have been fragmented, manual, and frustrating. Staff spend 20+ minutes verifying eligibility through phone calls. Treatment estimates rely on outdated fee schedules and guesswork. Claims sit in queues waiting for manual attachments. Payment posting requires hours of reconciliation. Denial management means paying staff to chase payments that should have been collected correctly the first time. This inefficiency is compounded by outdated systems and siloed processes, making it difficult to capture real-time data and track performance across multiple locations. As a result, DSOs struggle to gain a clear picture of their financial health, making it nearly impossible to make informed, strategic decisions in a timely manner. The promise of automation and AI Enter AI and automation. By automating key elements of the revenue cycle, from eligibility verification and claims processing to payment posting and denial management, DSOs can drastically reduce the administrative burden placed on staff. This not only improves efficiency but also reduces human error, speeding up the billing process and improving cash flow. For example, automation can verify insurance eligibility in real time before treatment begins, reducing the risk of unexpected patient balances and enabling more accurate treatment plans. Claims processed through AI-driven workflows can be automatically scrubbed for errors, reducing the likelihood of denials and the need for rework. This means faster collections, fewer denied claims, and a smoother patient experience, which ultimately results in better financial outcomes for practices. Automation can also help DSOs scale their operations without hiring additional staff. With many DSOs already facing labor shortages, automation allows them to do more with less. For example, automated denial management systems can track claims and identify trends in real time, ensuring swift, consistent follow-up without manual intervention. This is a game changer for practices looking to expand while managing costs effectively. Hidden revenue and reducing burnout As a CFO, I measure investments in what they unlock, protect, and enable. RCM automation delivers on all three. Reducing write-offs by 1% can mean hundreds of thousands for midsized DSOs. Improving collections from 95% to 98% expands margins without adding chairs or providers. You also protect your people. By automating routine tasks, teams are freed up to focus on more strategic and value-added activities, such as improving patient engagement and optimizing practice performance. Staff who are no longer bogged down by manual data entry and claim follow-ups can redirect their efforts toward patient care, leading to a more satisfied workforce and a more efficient practice. That efficiency becomes critical as you scale. Manual processes don't scale. Try doubling your location count without doubling your RCM headcount, and you'll see what I mean. Automated systems, on the other hand, handle volume growth with minimal incremental cost while providing the enterprise visibility investors expect. What DSOs need to know before implementing automation Here's the myth: AI-driven RCM implementation is too disruptive, too complex, too risky. The reality? That's what your competitors said last year … right before they automated their revenue cycle and left you behind. Yes, integration takes planning. However, with the right approach and the right technology partner, these challenges can be mitigated. To get the most out of RCM automation, DSOs should focus on a few key areas: Integration. Ensuring that the automation tools can seamlessly integrate with existing practice management software and other key systems is critical. Centralizing data from all locations into a single cloud-based system can enhance visibility and support more efficient management of the revenue cycle.

Customization. Not all practices are alike, and neither are their RCM needs. A good automation solution should be flexible enough to tailor its features to the organization's specific workflows and goals, minimizing disruption during implementation and ensuring long-term success.

Training. Successful automation adoption depends on effective change management. Offering role-specific training that demonstrates how automation will alleviate administrative burdens and improve job satisfaction is key to gaining staff buy-in. The cost of waiting Every month you delay is a month you pay the "waiting tax” -- lost revenue, inefficient operations, and mounting competitive disadvantage. Your competitors are automating. Your staff is burning out. Your investors are asking harder questions about operational efficiency. The dental organizations that will thrive are the ones that have modernized their financial infrastructure, eliminated revenue leakage, and built scalable operations. As CFOs, we can't control insurance policies or labor markets. But we can control whether our organizations operate efficiently. So, will you modernize RCM proactively, on your own terms, or reactively after the damage is done? Choose wisely. Your margins depend on it. Stephen Fong is the chief financial officer of Planet DDS. As CFO, Fong oversees strategic finance, business analytics, accounting, financial operations, and legal functions. One key strategy is the use of cloud-based infrastructure. By leveraging cloud service providers, companies reduce the need for physical servers and in-house IT management. Organizations are also focusing on subscription-based revenue models. Instead of one-time software sales, many mental health platforms operate on monthly or annual subscription plans. This ensures predictable cash flow and improves financial stability.

Partnerships are another way to manage costs. Mental health software companies collaborate with hospitals, insurance providers, employers, and educational institutions. One of the biggest challenges is data privacy and cybersecurity risk. Mental health data is highly sensitive. Another major challenge is regulatory uncertainty, especially regarding artificial intelligence (AI)-based tools. Many mental health platforms use AI for assessments, chatbots, and predictive analytics. However, regulations for AI in healthcare are still evolving. Companies must ensure clinical validation, transparency, and ethical use of algorithms. Delays in regulatory approvals can slow product launches.

Clinical credibility and evidence validation also remain key concerns. Some mental health apps enter the market without strong scientific backing. Healthcare professionals may hesitate to recommend solutions that lack peer-reviewed studies or proven outcomes. Without evidence-based validation, adoption among hospitals and clinics can remain limited.

Factors such as workplace stress, social pressures, and aging populations increase mental health impacts which surge the need for accessible support systems.

Telehealth is likely to remain a permanent component of healthcare delivery. Patients expect flexible and remote options for therapy and counseling. Integration with wearable devices and real-time monitoring systems will also enhance preventive care. Early detection models can reduce hospitalization rates and improve long-term patient outcomes. This growth is supported by increasing consolidation in dental practices and the adoption of innovative platforms designed to enhance patient care and operational efficiency. Let's explore the market's current scale, key drivers, leading players, emerging trends, and segment highlights shaping this evolving industry.



Projected Growth and Valuation of the Dental Service Organization Market

The dental service organization market is expected to experience rapid growth, reaching a valuation of $379.41 billion by 2030. This forecast is based on a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 15.8%. Several factors contribute to this surge, including the ongoing consolidation of dental practices into larger networks and the rising demand for scalable, integrated dental service platforms. Additionally, the growing use of tele-dentistry services and data-driven strategies for patient acquisition are further fueling market expansion. The integration of AI-based diagnostic tools also plays a crucial role in enhancing both patient outcomes and operational processes.

What Is Driving the Dental Service Organization Market Expansion

One major influence behind the market's growth is the increasing shift toward centralized practice management models. This approach allows for better coordination across multiple locations, providing streamlined workflows and improved patient experiences. Moreover, dental service organizations are embracing AI-driven systems for scheduling and billing, which reduce administrative burdens and optimize resource allocation.



Another important factor is the widespread adoption of digital patient records. These systems facilitate easier data sharing and integration across specialties, enabling multi-specialty dental networks to deliver comprehensive care. The emphasis on operational efficiency and standardization is helping organizations scale more effectively while maintaining high-quality services.

https://www.thebusinessresearchcompany.com/report/dental-service-organization-market-report?utm_source=OpenPR&utm_medium=Paid&utm_campaign=Feb_PR



Key Players Leading the Dental Service Organization Market

The dental service organization market features several prominent companies that dominate the space, such as Heartland Dental LLC, Aspen Dental Management Inc., Smile Brands Inc., Western Dental Services Inc., and Dental Care Alliance LLC. Other notable players include Great Expressions Dental Centers LLC, Dykema Gossett PLLC, Affordable Dentures & Implants LLC, MB2 Dental Solutions LLC, InterDent Service Corporation, Guardian Dentistry Partners LLC, Benevis LLC, Specialty1 Partners LLC, Pacific Dental Services LLC, Bluetree Dental LLC, iDental Group LLC, Affordable Care LLC, Lollipop Dental LLC, Straine Dental Management LLC, and Family Dental Care LLC.



Expanding Networks Through Strategic Partnerships

In June 2025, Innovate 32, a US-based dental services organization, partnered with Fort Bend Dental to broaden its affiliated practice network within Texas. This collaboration aims to strengthen their regional footprint, enhance operational support systems, and improve access to quality dental care by leveraging shared resources and centralized management. Fort Bend Dental is known for offering comprehensive oral healthcare services across the United States.



Technological Innovations Driving New Opportunities in the Market

Leading companies in the dental service organization market are prioritizing technological advancements, particularly the use of integrated cloud-based practice management platforms. These systems enable dental organizations to efficiently oversee multiple locations by consolidating administrative, financial, clinical, and patient engagement processes into one digital infrastructure. For example, in February 2024, US-based dental technology firm Planet DDS introduced Denticon Reimagined, an enhanced cloud platform designed specifically for large dental groups and DSOs. This platform boasts advanced analytics capabilities for real-time performance monitoring, built-in patient communication tools, and scalable architecture that supports centralized billing, scheduling, and reporting across numerous sites.



Major Segments Representing the Dental Service Organization Market

This market can be broken down into several key segments:

1) Type of Services: General Dentistry, Pediatric Dentistry, Orthodontics, Oral Maxillofacial Surgery, Periodontics, Cosmetic Dentistry, Endodontics, Prosthodontics

2) Practice Models: Single Specialty, Multi-Specialty, Corporate Owned, Independent Practitioner Networks, Franchise Models

3) Patient Demographics: Pediatric, Adult, Geriatric, Special Needs, Preventive Care Patients

4) Technology Utilization: Traditional Practices, Digital Records Management, Treatment Planning Software, Tele-dentistry, 3D Imaging and Printing, AI-Driven Diagnostics

5) End-Users: General Dentists, Dental Surgeons, and Specialists



Detailed Subsegments Within the Main Categories

The general dentistry segment includes services such as preventive dental care, routine exams, fillings and restorations, oral health education, and simple tooth extractions. Pediatric dentistry covers infant oral health, preventive care for children, restorative services, behavior management, and special needs care. Orthodontics features treatments like metal braces, ceramic braces, clear aligner therapy, lingual orthodontics, and early interceptive care. Oral maxillofacial surgery encompasses tooth extraction, implant surgery, corrective jaw surgery, trauma surgery, and oral pathology treatment. Periodontics involves gum disease treatment, scaling and root planing, periodontal surgery, gum grafting, and implant maintenance. Cosmetic dentistry includes teeth whitening, veneers, bonding, smile makeovers, and aesthetic contouring. Endodontics covers root canals, retreatment, apical surgery, trauma management, and pulp therapy. The prosthodontics segment includes crowns, bridges, complete and partial dentures, as well as implant-supported prosthetics.



This comprehensive breakdown highlights how the dental service organization market caters to a wide array of patient needs and utilizes advanced technologies to improve care delivery and operational efficiency.

data.author: Dentistry Today
data.full_text:
Industry News Planet DDS Expands Access to CareCredit Financing

Synchrony, a leading consumer financial services company, today announced an expanded strategic partnership with Planet DDS that helps orthodontic and dental practices simplify patient financing and makes it easier for patients to move forward with care. In the U.S., over 6 million patients currently receive orthodontic care across an estimated 15,000+ practices nationwide.i Through the integration of CareCredit into Planet DDS’s Cloud 9 orthodontic practice management platform—which serves approximately 2,500+ orthodontic practices and millions of patients nationwide—practices will soon be able to embed financing directly into their workflows, marking Synchrony’s first-ever integration with an orthodontic-specific practice management system. “For Dental Support Organizations (DSOs) and growing practices, the ability to scale hinges on having efficient, connected systems,” said Sonia Williams, Senior Vice President and General Manager, Dental, Synchrony. “Our expanded partnership with Planet DDS is designed to power that efficiency. By integrating CareCredit into their core software, we help practices operate more effectively and strengthen how they connect with patients about their financing options. Planet DDS Introduces AI Voice Perio to Bring Consistent, Scalable Perio Charting to DSOs

Share

The first AI and voice-powered perio system built into Denticon to ensure consistent, scalable clinical data for DSOs

IRVINE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Planet DDS today announced the launch of AI Voice Perio, the first voice-powered periodontal charting system built within Denticon. Designed specifically for DSOs and multi-location dental groups, this hands-free, voice-activated solution addresses a critical operational challenge: ensuring consistent, reliable perio data across locations without introducing fragmentation or operational overhead as organizations scale. AI Voice Perio captures periodontal measurements in real-time during the exam, eliminating the need for manual data entry and reducing interruptions. The system records voice commands directly into Denticon’s perio fields, ensuring reliable, consistent data that is stored automatically in patient records. “Scaling clinical operations without losing consistency is one of the hardest challenges DSOs face,” said Eric Giesecke, CEO of Planet DDS. “AI Voice Perio simplifies periodontal exams for clinicians and helps organizations capture consistent, reliable data as they grow. This gives clinical leaders standardized perio data they can trust for clinical oversight, training, and compliance.” The Future of Periodontal Exams By using a standardized voice-driven structure, AI Voice Perio ensures that exams are performed the same way each time, regardless of location or clinician. This results in comparable data over time, allowing DSOs to confidently build patient histories, track clinical trends, and maintain high-quality records as their practices grow. Key Features of AI Voice Perio: Voice-activated charting: Hygienists speak directly into Denticon’s system to record measurements, eliminating the need for manual typing or data entry. Built into Denticon: AI Voice Perio operates directly in Denticon’s clinical data model, ensuring consistency and governance without added reconciliation. Real-time corrections: Hygienists can make voice corrections during exams without interrupting the flow of the appointment. Standardized data capture: Ensures consistency in periodontal charting across practices, eliminating discrepancies caused by individual clinician preferences. Oral Health Report Cards: Results are saved in the patient record, providing longitudinal visibility of periodontal health. How AI Voice Perio Benefits DSOs DSOs and multi-location practices across the country are already experiencing the significant benefits of AI Voice Perio, with improved efficiency and consistency in their periodontal exams. “The feedback we’ve received on AI Voice Perio has been extremely positive. Adoption has been straightforward, and it makes periodontal exams easier,” said Etta Bourne, Vice President of System Integrations at Dental365. “It simplifies the workflow, allows hygienists to work more independently, and keeps everything in one system so they can stay focused on the patient instead of the process.” AI Voice Perio is now available to Denticon customers. Throughout 2026, Planet DDS will continue expanding its AI-powered clinical capabilities while working with partners across the DentalOS™ ecosystem to reduce operational complexity and improve care consistency as dental organizations scale. data.title: Coast Dental Selects Denticon for Operational Growth
data.ai_summary: Coast Dental, a dental organization with 88 locations in the US, selected Denticon by Planet DDS to support operational growth and scalability. The platform will enable Coast Dental to improve efficiency, interoperability, and support future expansion across its practices in Florida, Georgia, and Texas.
data.author: Dentistry Today
data.full_text:
Coast Dental, a patient-centric dental organization with 88 locations across the United States, has selected Denticon by Planet DDS to support operational consistency, interoperability, and scalability.

A Leading Dental Support Organization Focused on Patient Experience

Founded in 1992 by Adam Diasti, DDS, and Derek Diasti, Coast Dental is one of the largest dental support organizations in the United States, supporting practices in Florida, Georgia, and Texas, serving approximately one million patients and delivering more than 600,000 patient visits annually.

Coast Dental remains rooted in a belief that every dental visit should be a great experience, emphasizing a welcoming, patient-focused approach that builds trust and supports both short-term and long-term oral health goals.

Selecting a Scalable System of Record

Already leveraging Apteryx XVWeb by Planet DDS for imaging, Coast Dental sought a scalable practice management system of record that could support general and specialty dentistry workflows while maintaining operational simplicity for its more than 800 team members.

“We wanted a platform that could support our teams across all locations and give us confidence as we continue to grow,” said Derek Diasti, CEO of Coast Dental. “Denticon, along with the DentalOS open API platform, stood out as the foundation that will allow us to continue investing in our people, our practices, and the patient experience.”

Building for Long-Term Growth and Flexibility

As Coast Dental evaluated how best to support its next phase of growth, leadership looked for a platform that could evolve alongside the organization. Denticon’s enterprise-grade architecture, interoperability, and support for automation and AI-driven efficiency aligned with that direction, providing a unified foundation for both current operations and future innovation.

With open APIs and a forward-looking roadmap, Denticon gives Coast Dental the flexibility to build on its in-house capabilities while reducing administrative work and operational friction.

“Coast Dental approached this decision with a clear focus on their patients, their teams, and their future,” said Mike Huffaker, Chief Revenue Officer at Planet DDS. “They were looking for a system built to handle real enterprise complexity while remaining adaptable as their organization evolves. We’re proud to support Coast Dental as they build on that foundation.”

A Connected Technology Foundation

With Denticon as its core practice management platform, supported by Planet DDS Pay, Denticon Practice Analytics, AI Assist, and XVWeb for imaging, Coast Dental is building a connected technology foundation designed to scale with its team members and patients.

In summary, Coast Dental’s selection of Denticon establishes a scalable, cloud-based practice management foundation that supports operational consistency, interoperability, and long-term growth across its 88 locations.

Resources:

For more information about Denticon and Planet DDS, visit www.planetdds.com.

About Coast Dental

Headquartered in Tampa, FL, Coast Dental owns and operates 88 dental practices across Florida, Georgia, and Texas. The company is dedicated to delivering the best in dental care while ensuring the utmost comfort and convenience for patients. Coast Dental’s focus on exceptional service extends to its approach to employee welfare, making it a leader in both patient care and workplace satisfaction.

Learn more at www.coastdental.com.

About Planet DDS

Dental software is broken. We aim to fix it. As a partner in growth for DSOs and dental groups, Planet DDS delivers a cloud-based AI platform designed to scale alongside growing organizations. Powered by DentalOS™ with AI, Planet DDS is built on connection—connecting people, partners, and technology across an open ecosystem that includes Denticon Practice Management, Cloud 9 Ortho Practice Management, and Apteryx Cloud Imaging.

Trusted by leading DSOs and emerging dental groups nationwide, Planet DDS enables 13,000+ practices and 118,000 users to move beyond outdated legacy software with seamless integrations, optimized workflows, and scalable technology built for growth.

This page contains press release content distributed by XPR Media. Members of the editorial and news staff of the USA TODAY Network were not involved in the creation of this content. DentTracks Strengthens Its AI-Powered Dental Ecosystem With Deep PMS Integrations and Global Technology Partnerships EIN Newswire AI-powered, all-in-one dental business management ecosystem Our mission at DentTracks is to bring clarity and accountability to dental practices by unifying operations and finances, giving leaders real-time insight into what’s happening and what to do next.” — Dr. Vajahat Yar Khan, Founder & CEO, DentTracks HOUSTON, TX, UNITED STATES, January 6, 2026 /EINPresswire.com/ — DentTracks, an AI-powered, all-in-one dental business management ecosystem, today announced a significant expansion of its platform through deeper Practice Management Software integrations, enhanced AI-driven capabilities such as Single Login and AI Voice Notes, and a growing network of global enterprise technology partners. Built for modern dental organizations, DSOs, and multi-location dental groups, DentTracks unifies clinical, operational, financial, and patient-experience intelligence into a single system without disrupting existing PMS workflows or increasing staff complexity. Comprehensive PMS Integrations for Seamless Practice Operations DentTracks offers deep, bi-directional integrations with leading dental PMS platforms, enabling real-time data synchronization, workflow automation, and advanced analytics across front desk, clinical, and billing operations. Supported PMS integrations include:

‣ Dentrix Ascend

‣ Dentrix

‣ Dentrix Enterprise

‣ Open Dental Software

‣ Eaglesoft by Patterson Dental

‣ Tab32

‣ Planet DDS and Denticon These integrations eliminate manual data handling, reduce operational blind spots, and provide unified visibility across single-location practices, group practices, and DSOs. Dental teams can continue using their existing PMS while DentTracks works silently in the background to transform raw data into actionable intelligence. Single Login Experience Across the Dental Tech Stack One of the most common frustrations in dental operations is managing multiple software logins across PMS, communication tools, payments, analytics, and reporting systems. DentTracks solves this with a Single Login experience that enables authorized users to securely access insights, dashboards, workflows, and integrated systems through a single, unified interface. This reduces cognitive load for staff, improves adoption, and significantly enhances operational efficiency at scale, especially for DSOs and multi-location groups. AI Voice Notes That Work for Dentists and Teams DentTracks introduces AI Voice Notes to help dentists and staff capture critical information without interrupting clinical or administrative workflows.

With AI Voice Notes, users can: ‣ Dictate operational or clinical observations in real time
